Title: Distinct Profiles of Run-to-Run Score Reliability and Expert-Panel Alignment Across Four LLM Evaluators of Simulated Japanese-Language AI-to-AI Counseling
Design: 4 evaluator systems x 18 transcripts x 3 repeated scorings; 15 expert panel
Why it is a comparator: Closest true test-retest design: same system, same input, repeated. Shows run-to-run reliability and expert alignment are independent axes - high ICC did not predict closer expert agreement.

Title: LLM Judges as Raters: A Pre-Registered Audit of Severity, Halo, Reliability, and Version Instability in LLM Essay Scoring on Public Corpora
Design: 2,377 essays, 12 judges, 4 providers, 5 version contrasts, replicated cells
Why it is a comparator: Pre-registered replication estimate of within-judge self-consistency; also the only retrieved study measuring cross-version drift (severity shifts up to 133 points on a 0-1000 scale, one judge deprecated mid-study).

Title: Diagnosing Bias and Instability in LLM Evaluation: A Scalable Pairwise Meta-Evaluator
Design: 3,600+ pairwise comparisons, 5 open-weight models, 10 prompts, mirrored order
Reliability metric: Verdict reversal rate under mirrored order
Why it is a comparator: Highest single-model verdict instability retrieved, and peer-reviewed. Same judge, same pair, order swapped. Cross-judge consistency was 100% while within-judge reversal was 48.4% - agreement between judges says nothing about stability within one.

Title: Same Input, Different Scores: A Multi Model Study on the Inconsistency of LLM Judge
Design: 5 judge models, 2 temperature settings, repeated runs on identical inputs
Why it is a comparator: Establishes that temperature = 0 does not deliver determinism; completeness-type criteria fluctuate most. Relevant if GLM-5.2 verdicts were generated greedily and assumed reproducible.

Title: The Coin Flip Judge? Reliability and Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
Design: Repeated runs per question; paraphrase perturbation
Why it is a comparator: Per-pair within-judge flip rate - the direct unit-matched comparator to an implied per-pair disagreement. Paraphrasing changed the majority verdict on 25% of questions.

Title: TrustJudge: Inconsistencies of LLM-as-a-Judge and How to Alleviate Them
Why it is a comparator: Within-judge logical inconsistency on a single model, independent of any human reference.

Title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias
Why it is a comparator: Upper bound on achievable within-judge stability, and the dissociation result: test-retest >0.95 coexisting with position bias >0.10. High self-consistency does not imply low bias.

Title: trajectory-judge: What Outcome-Only LLM Judges Miss on Agent Trajectories
Design: 400 trajectories, 5 judge configurations incl. self-consistency ensemble
Why it is a comparator: Directly relevant remedy check: majority-voting a judge against itself did not fix the errors it makes, so repeat-and-vote is not a defensible fix for instability.
